constraints.text: Nineteen Plates of the Historical Sky

items.item: All eight spreads hold one grid and one caption architecture whether the plate is a sparse card or a lettered sheet.
Each caption sits in the bottom band of the type area with its four fields in the required order.
The five openers share one heading position, thumbnail treatment and folio, and the two index spreads use one matching label system.
Openers and index spreads carry the chapter names as fixed in the letter and the plates assigned to each.
The three cover states show one cover design and belong to the selected direction.
Title and descriptor appear in every state and the title stays legible at thumbnail size.

dqRubric.naRules: Do not judge material texture or lighting on the flat page files (cover flat, direction boards, openers, plate spreads and index spreads, which are print-plane layouts) and do not judge the engraving quality, colour or condition of the nineteen supplied historical plates, which are given artwork; only cover-object is judged as a lit physical object.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

On the flat, read the three panels separately. The front panel must carry both the title and the descriptor line. The spine panel must carry the imprint with its letters running so the words are read from the head down to the foot when the book stands upright; bottom-to-top or horizontally stacked letters fail. The back panel must hold a machine-style barcode block with the ISBN digits, placed in its lower right quadrant and clearly wider than tall in roughly a 40:25 ratio; a barcode centred, on the front, or square/portrait in proportion fails. Exact millimetre measurement is not expected — position and proportion are the evidence.

In each spread's caption block the four items must be readable in the stated sequence, top to bottom or left to right, with the credit last. The wording of the collection title, the accession number and the date-and-maker text must agree with the record for that plate (plate-03 = 46447i, plate-10 = 46168i, plate-18 = 46180i). Failure: a field missing, two fields swapped, an accession number belonging to a different plate, a shortened or paraphrased collection title, or a date or maker not in the record. Typographic styling of the fields (weight, italic, small caps, line breaks, separating rules) is free.

Where the record has no year or no maker, the caption must show the standing placeholder wording rather than an empty slot, a dash, 'unknown', 'n.d.', 'anon.' or a guessed date. The plate-03 caption needs the date placeholder and the maker names from the record; the plate-10 caption needs both placeholders; the plate-18 caption needs the maker placeholder and its bracketed place. Inventing a year or an engraver for any of these is a failure.

Each caption must end with the source name and the rights wording together, as the last of the four items. Either one alone, a different rights phrase (CC0, 'copyright free', 'public domain' in other words), or the credit floated away from the caption into a folio or margin is a failure. A separator between the two (dash, bullet, slash, new line) is allowed.

Compare the pages as a group. Plate images, headings, thumbnails and caption text must start and stop on a repeating vertical structure that reads as six equal columns with narrow gutters; elements may span several columns but must not cut a column in half differently on each page. The outer margin must read narrower than the foot margin, and those margins must be the same width on every page in the set. Every caption block must sit as a band at the bottom of the type area, occupying roughly the lowest eighth of it and never rising into the middle of the page or dropping below the foot margin. Failure: one page on a visibly different column count or margin set, or a caption floated beside or above the plate.

Across the delivered pages, the designer's own ink — rules, headings, folios, caption type, panels, cover ground — must read as one dark desaturated navy of the same hue on every file. The reproduced historical plates keep their own colour and are not judged. Failure: a page whose structural ink drifts to black, mid blue, warm brown or another accent hue, or a set where the navy is visibly a different colour from file to file.

Read the sheet for stated facts. It must identify exactly one of the three direction boards as the chosen one, by a name or number a reader can tie to a delivered board, and it must state the trim, the extent, the spine width, the column count with its column measure, and list the four caption items in their required sequence. Failure: no direction named, two directions named as selected, a figure contradicting the letter, or the caption fields listed out of order or incompletely.

Identify the chosen board from the specification sheet, then check every finished page against it: openers, spreads, index spreads and cover states must share that board's type family, caption treatment, rule work and image framing. Refinement is allowed. Failure: any group of pages built on a rejected board's treatment, or the openers following one board while the spreads follow another.

Find the four production values in the presentation document and set them beside the specification sheet. Each must be repeated with the same numbers and the same hex string. Failure: a value rounded, re-expressed in a different unit that changes it, a hex code altered by even one character, a different column count or measure, or a value present on the sheet and absent from the document.

The document must run to eight pages or more, name the chosen direction on its first page, and show each delivered cover state, each of the five openers, each of the eight spreads and both index spreads as artwork on its pages. Failure: fewer than eight pages, the direction not named on page one, any listed file missing, or substitute artwork that differs from what was delivered.

All three states must carry the title and the descriptor line and read as one cover. In the thumbnail state the title must still be separable word by word at that reduced width — if it collapses into a grey texture the state fails, and dropping the descriptor from the thumbnail is also a failure. The object state must show a bound copy with front cover and spine, resting on the supplied display table surface under the same daylight direction as the input photograph; a floating book, a studio backdrop, a different room, or relit contradictory shadows fail.

Watch the whole clip and check the sequence: it opens on the cover, passes two of the delivered chapter openers, and ends on the two text-heavy spreads, all shown as the delivered artwork. Failure: a missing station in that order, pages that are not delivered files, or a clip far off twelve seconds. Which two openers are used is the designer's choice.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Each board must set both the sparse card and the caption-heavy comet plate, so the pair can be judged against each other. The three boards must differ in a way an editor could choose between — caption placement, column use, image scale, type hierarchy — not merely in colour or in a moved rule. Failure: a board setting only one of the two plates, a board substituting another plate, or boards so alike that no decision is offered.

For each of these spreads, read the caption and compare with the record for that plate: title wording, accession number and the catalogue date-and-place text must all belong to the plate pictured, in the required sequence. The Venetian plate's date line must keep its bracketed English gloss, its publisher and its year, and the 1786 London plate must carry its place-and-year line as recorded. Failure: an accession number or title borrowed from a neighbouring plate, a translated or tidied date line, a dropped bracket or year, or fields out of order.

Check the last line of each caption: source name and rights wording together, as the closing item, on every one of these spreads. The plate-10 caption must additionally show both standing placeholders, since neither year nor maker is recorded for it. Failure: the credit on some spreads only, the rights label replaced by other licence wording, the credit placed above the record fields, or plate-10 carrying a guessed date or engraver.

Both spreads must name the same constellation in readable type, and each must carry a pointer to the other page by the other plate's accession number, so an editor can follow the coloured card to the line projection and back. Failure: only one of the two carrying a pointer, a pointer quoting its own accession number, a pointer using a page number or chapter name with no accession number, or the constellation named on one spread only. The wording and position of the pointer are the designer's choice.

Count thumbnails per opener against its chapter's plate count (nine, two, three, two, three) and confirm each opener shows only its own chapter's plates; then confirm the two index spreads between them cover all nineteen, so each plate is found on an opener and on an index. Then compare the three spreads: the sparse card and the two dense sheets must sit on the same column measure and put their captions in the same bottom band, with density absorbed by more lines or smaller settings, not by a wider measure or a taller caption area. The five openers must place their chapter heading in the same spot and treat the page number identically. Failure: a wrong thumbnail count, a plate missing from the openers or from the indexes, a dense spread on its own measure or with a caption climbing the page, or an opener whose heading jumps position.

The first index spread must hold the first ten plates as thumbnails in accession-number sequence; the second must hold the remaining nine in collection-title sequence. Check a few neighbouring entries to confirm the stated sequence actually holds and that the two spreads share one thumbnail and label treatment. Failure: a plate on the wrong spread, a plate on both or on neither, thumbnails in arbitrary order, or labels that do not show the value the sequence is built on.

All eight spreads hold one grid and one caption architecture whether the plate is a sparse card or a lettered sheet. Each caption sits in the bottom band of the type area with its four fields in the required order.

The five openers share one heading position, thumbnail treatment and folio, and the two index spreads use one matching label system. Openers and index spreads carry the chapter names as fixed in the letter and the plates assigned to each.
The three cover states show one cover design and belong to the selected direction. Title and descriptor appear in every state and the title stays legible at thumbnail size.
